summary: Finds the values present in every one of the given arrays, deduplicated and in the first array's order.
description:
Order comes from the first array, and the result is deduplicated: a value repeated there appears once. Values are
compared with `SameValueZero`, the rule a `Set` uses, so `NaN` intersects with `NaN` — which a comparison by `===`
never does — and `-0` matches `0`.

The arrays after the first each become a set once, and the first is then walked a single time. The cost is linear in
the total input rather than the nested scan a hand-written version usually ends up being. The inputs are not
modified.
Called with a single array, `intersect` returns its unique values; called with none, it returns `[]`.

params.arrays: The arrays to intersect. Left untouched.

returns: a new array of the shared values, in the order of the first array, without duplicates.

throws.TypeError: Any argument is not an array.

examples.title: Finding the rows two sheets have in common
examples.body:
<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="intersect.ts" include-symbol="findSharedIds"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function findSharedIds(active, billed) {
  const left = active.getRange("A2:A").getValues().flat();
  const right = billed.getRange("A2:A").getValues().flat();
  return intersect(left, right);
}
</code-block>

examples.title: Deduplication and edge cases
examples.body:
```javascript
intersect([1, 1, 2], [1, 2]); // => [1, 2] — the result is deduplicated
intersect([NaN], [NaN]); // => [NaN]
intersect([1, 2]); // => [1, 2] — a single array, deduplicated
intersect(); // => []
```
